title: Drive the Thoughts: Runtime Monitoring of VLA Reasoning-Trajectory Consistency
abstract: arXiv:2608.29583v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) operate in complex environments where failures are consequential. Sophisticated machine learning models for perception and planning are key to overcoming at least part of that complexity, but their black-box nature complicates validation and verification (V&V). The recent integration of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models into AVs introduces a unique opportunity: besides generating trajectories, these models produce an explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) explaining their underlying rationale. This CoT provides a rich specification to cross-check model outputs and detect inconsistencies that may expose unsafe or unintended behavior. translated_title: 驱动思维：VLA推理-轨迹一致性的运行时监控
translated_abstract: 自动驾驶汽车（AV）在复杂环境中运行，一旦发生故障后果严重。用于感知与规划的先进机器学习模型是克服至少部分复杂性的关键，但其黑盒特性使验证与确认（V&V）变得困难。近期将视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型集成到自动驾驶汽车中带来了独特机遇：除了生成轨迹之外，这些模型还会产生显式的思维链（CoT）来解释其底层推理依据。该思维链为交叉检验模型输出、检测可能暴露不安全或非预期行为的不一致性提供了丰富的规范。本文评估了来自近期开放驾驶VLA模型的思维链能否支持此类监控。我们构建了DriveAlignBench，这是一个源自NVIDIA Alpamayo 1.5自动驾驶VLA的专用数据集，包含150对思维链-轨迹对，并对其进行了人工标注，涵盖可靠性、轨迹一致性以及……
tldr: 本文提出DriveAlignBench数据集，通过运行时监控VLA模型思维链推理与生成轨迹之间的一致性，来检测自动驾驶系统中潜在的不安全行为。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DriveAlignBench, a dataset enabling runtime monitoring of the consistency between VLA chain-of-thought reasoning and generated trajectories to detect potentially unsafe behaviors in autonomous vehicles.
